title: 2004 HMMT February Guts Problem 6
statement: Find the smallest integer \(n\) such that \(\sqrt{n+99}-\sqrt{n}<1\).

solutions.text:
2402
This is equivalent to

\[\begin{aligned}
\sqrt{n+99} & <\sqrt{n}+1 \\
n+99 & <n+1+2 \sqrt{n} \\
49 & <\sqrt{n}
\end{aligned}\]

So the smallest integer \(n\) with this property is \(49^{2}+1=2402\).
